evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says: 'This should take about five to ten minutes of your time so we can build an accurate quote you can depend on, sounds good.' — time-boxed and promise made, but customer response is ambiguous ('Yeah. Yes, that's all we gotta do...') and rep does not wait for a clear yes before moving forward.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Moving day: 'Probably the second week of October' — asked and answered. Current location: '8012 enter court, Justin, 78729' — asked and answered. Destination city: never asked. Home size: '124 bedrooms' [likely '1-2 bedrooms']; square footage unknown per customer. Rep gathered name (Ron Romeo), email, phone, and learned it's a 2-story house with 4 bedrooms, living room, kitchen; rep did not ask for destination city or confirm square footage.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep asks: 'Do you have any concerns or do you have any important things that you wanted to answer during this call today?' — asked, but only after probing began (name, email, how you heard about us were already asked). Customer raises concern about glass items and diplomas being damaged.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises concern: 'I have glass on top of like, re, or something and people are smashing. So, I have concerns about that and some diplomas like.' Rep responds: 'Okay. Alright. Okay, one sec.' — no follow-up question, no 'tell me more about that,' rep pivots immediately to address probing.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: Rep does not reflect back or summarize the customer's concerns. No confirmation of what was heard.
evidence_quotes.walkthrough_offer: Rep correctly identifies the triggering factor: 'Oh normally if this, if that's more than 1700 we normally do a virtual walkthrough so you can let us know what are the things that we are moving in?' — walkthrough branch is triggered and offered appropriately when customer indicates uncertainty about room count and items being moved.

top_strength: Rep correctly identified and routed this as a walkthrough-scheduler call, recognizing the home size and item complexity warranted a virtual walkthrough rather than a phone-based quote.
coaching_note: Probe for concerns before jumping into routine data collection — ask 'their agenda' immediately after the quid pro quo, not after you've already asked for name and email, and always follow up when a customer raises a concern (here: the fragile items) with at least one clarifying question before moving on.
